title: Reading Drill — Monitoring quiet time in a gallery — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Monitoring quiet time in a gallery — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Ravensmere, work on large visitor groups masking quiet spoken labels had already produced a small collection of listening tests. The gallery attendant used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the number of audible labels.

**B** The group kept spaced entry times for the new trial, which was planned to run for seven weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that tour guide amplification should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
